sources.title: European spiny lobster (Palinurus elephas) - MarLIN - The Marine Life Information Network
sources.scope: Selected actual Naturalis/FAO species diagnosis read: distinct transverse abdominal grooves, longitudinal leg streaks, paired white spots on somites2–5 and single posteromedian spot6; male P1 spine sex-specific. Generic narrow unarmed plate and short antennules distinguished from Panulirus. No measured morphology, historical fisheries or physiological parameters.

sources.title: Naturalis/FAO — Palinurus genus diagnosis
sources.scope: Selected generic diagnosis, not measured species-specific proportions: unarmed narrow antennular plate, short flagella of antennules, dentate supraorbital horns, flexible long second antennae and first legs without great pincers.

sources.title: Holthuis1991 FAO — Palinurus elephas diagnosis and figure224
sources.scope: Actual selected PDFpage124 printed115 key and page128 printed119 Fig224 examined; no full-volume review. The species figure and antennular-plate detail guide the unarmed narrow plate, curved dentate horns, serial pleurae and long tapered antennae. Historical fisheries and ranges are not quantitative current data.

retrieval.accessMethod: Selected actual PDF text and rendered figure

findings.shape: Continuous spined carapace, separate visible eye ends, curved dentate supraorbital horns, narrow unarmed antennular plate, shorter antennules, six overlapping grooved abdominal plates with selected paired pale spots, five-part tail fan and ten articulated non-chelate walking limbs replace the oval/rod draft.
findings.surface: Red-brown original numerical cuticle with a subdued pale flank, irregularly spaced seated spines, longitudinal leg streaks, paired spots on somites2–5 and a single posterior spot6. Tapered strong antennae and fine fan-ray cues remain on the same model through all actions.
findings.movement: A short authored forward bout with fixed-length limbs and ground-fixed support contacts; local antenna/antennule search gestures, quiet supported rest and mild serial abdominal/fan flex. No full feeding, escape trajectory, forces, calibrated stride or sensory/physiological simulation.
findings.evidenceScope: The authentic JoJan CC BY3.0 Monaco aquarium photograph was viewed alongside selected Naturalis/FAO species/genus diagnoses. Actual Holthuis1991 PDFpage128 printed119 Fig224 and its anterior-carapace detail were rendered and viewed; selected key text page124 printed115 distinguishes species-level groove/spot characters and male-specific P1 armature. The selected non-chelate final-leg form is not an independent determination of source-photo sex.
corrections: Moved eye ends outside the initial buried frontal surface and tapered blunt horn tips.
Replaced overly uniform pink cuticle with a darker red-brown dorsal surface and a quieter flank.
Removed the artificial pale frontal panel, reduced block-like mouth covers and replaced all55 affected captures.
Staggered and varied the initially gridded spines and moved paired pale spots away from the transverse grooves.
Revised finite-bout stopping to complete lifted recovery while keeping planted feet fixed; corrected contact flags near recovery endpoints and bound anatomy markers to retained groups.
findings.residual: Carapace/head proportions, fine spine coordinates and density, segment grooves, pleural contours, antennal joints, eye microanatomy, maxillipeds and optical properties remain simplified and unmeasured. Ten supported limbs and a mild local tail flex are educational articulation studies, not observed/fitted species kinematics. Female-specific final-leg chelation, sex-modified pleopods, complete mouthparts, internal organs and fluid/feeding functions are not reconstructed. The model is still partly stylized and does not represent every posture, stage or phenotype.

assessmentRubric.surface: Selected original numerical cuticle/pigment, not calibrated photoreal optics
assessmentRubric.movement: Working same-model support and partial articulation; natural gait/timing not measured

limits: Original qualitative educational reconstruction; proportions, cuticle optics, natural timing, joint limits, forces, feeding, sensing and physiology remain unmeasured. No independent specialist validation or accuracy percentage. Software support checks are not empirical biological validation.

Carapace/head proportions, fine spine coordinates and density, segment grooves, pleural contours, antennal joints, eye microanatomy, maxillipeds and optical properties remain simplified and unmeasured. Female-specific final-leg chelation, sex-modified pleopods, complete mouthparts, internal organs and fluid/feeding functions are not reconstructed. The model is still partly stylized and does not represent every posture, stage or phenotype.
